description: Overrides the normal voice chosen for a character in a specific story demo or story mission, and lets game phases preload the override voice cue sheets.

Id.simple: Row key for one voice-override rule.
Id.technical: FName row key. No behavioral read of this member was found in the available consumers; rows are collected wholesale from DTM.StoryVoiceOverrideDataTables (+0x8F0) and filtered by Id_StoryDemo and Id_Character. Export spells it ID.

Id_StoryDemo.simple: Story demo/mission ID that the override applies to.
Id_StoryDemo.technical: FName. The battle-story preload keeps rows whose value equals GameManager.StudioStoryMissionId_CE0. The unique-pair sequencer evaluator keeps rows whose value equals StudioStoryDemoId_CD8, falling back to StudioStoryDiagramDemoId_CF8 when the former is None, and skips all overrides while a result sequence (sequence type 2) is current.

Id_Character.simple: Target character whose voice is overridden.
Id_Character.technical: FName. The sequencer evaluator requires it to equal the resolved target character ID (and requires that ID to be non-None) before applying the override. Level-sequence asset preparation adds the override voice cue sheet for every row matching a character being prepared; the battle-story preload does not filter by character.

Id_Voice.technical: FName. The sequencer evaluator assigns this value as the chosen VoiceId before its normal unique-pair/group fallbacks, so a matching row wins. Preload paths resolve it in VoiceDataTable and add Voice.CueSheetName to the load list; a missing Voice row leaves no override voice/cue sheet.

notes: Loaded as a DataTable primary asset named StoryVoiceOverrideDataTable into DTM.StoryVoiceOverrideDataTables (+0x8F0).
The override is scoped by demo ID and (in the sequencer) character ID; it takes precedence over unique-pair voices and the common fallback group, except during result sequences.
The same table is used for cue-sheet preloading in two phase paths, one keyed only by story mission ID and one keyed only by character ID.

Sources are reconstructed retail C++; the unique-pair evaluator is byte-marked DIFF in status/verdicts.json:73124, so exact retail equivalence of that consumer is not byte-proven. Content is partial; no retail completeness claim.

usages.detail: Collects override rows to preload cue sheets for the current story mission.
Collects per-character override cue sheets during level-sequence preparation.
Unique-pair voice evaluation applies matching demo/character overrides.
Override wins before unique-pair and common fallback voice selection.
